title: Hyperscene (open canvas)
description: Generic data-driven composition. The JSON is the video. Layers (text/image/component/rect) with timed windows, kinetic splits, the cut kit (whip/punch/iris/...), WebGL shader stings (flash/burn/leak/grain/dissolve), theme bg-preset windows on canvas, global camera, captions.
note: data.theme drives palette/fonts/bg colours. Coordinates are px in the chosen orientation space (1080×1920 portrait, 1920×1080 landscape).

layerProps._source: the PROPS declarations beside each read (core/registry/props.js - core/layers/vocabulary.js)

aspect.label: Canvas aspect (overrides orientation). CLI --aspect a,b,c renders multiple in one pass.

destination.label: Where this ships. Decides the safe area: a phone feed paints chrome over the frame, a website does not. Default web (margin only).

idle.label: The film's DEFAULT idle: ambient motion every layer carries across its settled middle, so held frames read as confident rather than dead. One line opts the whole cast in; a layer's own `idle` overrides it, and `idle: "none"` on a layer opts that one back out. Off unless asked.

cameraBlur.label: CAMERA MOTION BLUR. A shutter exposes the SENSOR, so with this on every layer smears by its velocity RELATIVE TO THE CAMERA: a whip pan streaks the whole frame, and a layer whose own `motion` travels with the camera stays sharp because the two velocities cancel. Off by default. HOW MUCH is the film's `shutter` (degrees), and one layer opts out with `motionBlur: false`. Only the camera's x/y translation smears: a zoom (`s`) and a roll are radial and are deliberately not modelled.

shutter.label: MOTION BLUR for the whole film, as a camera states it: the SHUTTER ANGLE in degrees. 180 is the film standard (the frame exposed for half its duration), 360 is twice the smear, 90 halves it, and 0 turns the automatic blur off. Omitted, the engine keeps its own default of about 58 degrees. It is the default only: a layer overrides it with `motionBlur` (false opts out, a number sets its own shutter), and every blur is still velocity-derived off that layer's motion track.

tempo.label: Global pace dial. 1 (default) = unchanged, 0.85 = 15% slower, 1.2 = 20% faster. Scales every authored time in the scene (durations, starts, delays, camera legs, typing speed) by 1/tempo in one pass, resolved once in core/engine/expand.js before build and bake; footage and the audio bed play at their own native rate regardless. Refused outside 0.5-2 (core/engine/tempo.js): past that range a scene needs re-timing by hand, not a dial.

fps.label: Frame rate (default 30; use 60 for smoother fast motion)

energy.label: Film energy: the default speed curve for every cut and seam that names no timing. calm decelerates into place; brand is the house slow-fast-slow speed ramp; hype lands snappy and stops; tense accelerates away. An explicit timing on a cut always wins.

captionStyle.label: Word-timed caption treatment on the pop layout (core/type/captions.js). Optional per-line words:[{t0,t1}].

bg.label: Background windows (canvas, theme palette)
bg.hint: the backdrop is the largest area of the frame, so the engine will not pick it for you. Use `"bg": [{ "preset": "plain" }]` for a deliberately flat field, a living preset (dotmatrix · gradientWash · blobs · metallic · metallicSheen · aurora · …, each one a named recipe over the same vocabulary), `{ "base": {...}, "fx": [...] }` to compose that vocabulary yourself, or `{ "html": "…" }` to hand-author one. See docs backgrounds-and-images.

html.label: Hand-authored living background (raw HTML/CSS instead of a preset)

src.label: Path to a .html fragment holding that hand-authored background, instead of the inline `html` string (exactly one of the two)

tone.label: Is the hand-authored backdrop light or dark? (picks the default text ink)

from.label: Window start: seconds, OR a junction reference like "cut@1" so the joint owns the number. OMIT IT on EVERY window and the engine binds them to the film's cuts in order, one window per beat, which is how a backdrop changes without naming a boundary twice (core/timeline/junctions.js)

to.label: Window end: seconds, OR a junction reference like "cut@2". Omitted on every window = bound to the joints; see `from`

opts.label: Per-video tuning of THIS preset's fx. Meta knobs scale what the preset baked in: { intensity, dotAlpha, drift, grain }. Every other key is passed straight to the fx that reads it, so the fx's own parameters work by name (liquid: scale, speed, warp, edge0, edge1, gloss, res · dots: spacing, period, k, driftX, driftY · metallic: count, waves, glow, sweep · particles: count, speed, connectDist). A key this preset's fx do not read is an ERROR, and the message lists the ones they do.

base.label: Compose a backdrop yourself instead of naming a preset: the flat field under your `fx`. `{kind:"solid", color}` or `{kind:"linear"|"radial"|"conic", from, to, cx, cy, angle}`. Same shape a preset's own `build()` returns; write `fx` alongside it. One of `preset` / `base`+`fx` / `use` / `html`+`src` per window, never two.

fx.label: Compose a backdrop yourself: an ordered list of `{type, ...}` painters, the SAME vocabulary every preset is built from (core/backgrounds/fx.js) — type: dots|particles|aurora|softwash|spotlight|metallic|liquid|grain|gradientFill, each with its own parameters read straight off the painter. Paired with `base`; `opts` does not apply here, write the values directly.

seed.label: Vary the preset's positions/phase (default = hash of theme+preset, so brands differ)

use.label: use:"theme" → pull the brand’s own authored backdrop (themes/<name>.json bgDefault)

breathe.label: Slow scale pulse on the canvas while this window is active. Default OFF. `true` for the built-in feel (2% scale, ~18s period), or `{amp, period}` to tune it. A canvas-painted window only; a hand-authored (`html`) window has no effect to breathe.

cuts.label: INTERNAL: the lowered output of transitions[] (mech:"cut"). Never author this directly, write transitions[] and run `node harness/author/migrate-junctions.mjs` on an old file that still has one.

t.label: Cut time (s), or "beat:<n>" (bare, 0-based) pinning this cut to the nth beat of the film's music grid, resolved by core/beats/index.js once audio.beatSync loads it.

snap.label: false keeps this exact time when audio.beatSync is on. "beat"/"bar"/"downbeat" instead snaps THIS cut to that pulse regardless of audio.beatSync.bar's own default (core/beats/index.js).

cx.label: Origin x, PER CENT of the frame (core/cuts/index.js formats it as `%` and defaults to 50)

cy.label: Origin y, PER CENT of the frame (core/cuts/index.js formats it as `%` and defaults to 50)

dist.label: Travel distance in px for a directional cut

stings.label: INTERNAL: the lowered output of transitions[] (mech:"sting"). Never author this directly, write transitions[] and run `node harness/author/migrate-junctions.mjs` on an old file that still has one.

t.label: Center time (s), or "beat:<n>" (bare, 0-based) pinning it to the nth beat of the film's music grid (core/beats/index.js).

color.label: Tint hex (recolours the effect; omit for native colours)

colors.label: leak: up to 4 hex colours the leak is built from (seed only arranges them)

seams.label: INTERNAL: the lowered output of transitions[] (mech:"seam"). Never author this directly, write transitions[] and run `node harness/author/migrate-junctions.mjs` on an old file that still has one.

t.label: Seam start time (s), the window is [t, t+dur]. Or "beat:<n>" (bare, 0-based) pinning it to the nth beat of the film's music grid, resolved by core/beats/index.js once audio.beatSync loads it.

snap.label: false keeps this exact time when audio.beatSync is on. "beat"/"bar"/"downbeat" instead snaps THIS seam to that pulse regardless of audio.beatSync.bar's own default (core/beats/index.js).

fx.label: Transition (samples BOTH beats as textures). Basics: fade · dissolve · slide · push · uncover · wipe (dir-aware). Expressive: crossWarp · whipPan · sdfIris · dispersion · lens · flashWhite · cinematicZoom · portal.

dir.label: Travel direction: left|right|up|down, or a number of degrees (0=right, 90=up) for any angle. A bad string is refused at render (core/timeline/seams.js okDir), not by this schema, because a union type carries no enum check.

feather.label: Edge softness override for the edge-based units (wipe, irisRound, clockWipe, barnDoor, blindsWipe, burnThrough, lumaWipe). Omit for that unit's own baked default.

timing.label: Easing of the transition progress (default smooth = ease-in-out). linear = constant-speed (mechanical); smooth/out/snappy/pop/rush/brake/ramp shape the blend's velocity. Same curves as a scene cut's timing (core/cuts/index.js).

produced.label: Set false to OPT OUT of the produced baseline the engine injects by default (core/engine/produce.js): a living/brand-appropriate background, a gentle camera push, and sceneUnits on cut films. Additive only (never rewrites your layers). Absent = produced (rich by default); false = render exactly what the JSON declares. Any field you set explicitly (bg, cameraMove, sceneUnits) already overrides its part of the baseline.

sceneUnits.label: Make `cuts` move each BEAT as a WHOLE UNIT (the outgoing beat slides/pushes out while the incoming slides in, as separate scenes) instead of transforming the whole camera at once. Turns beat boundaries from a per-layer-fade slideshow into real scene swaps. Beats are the intervals between cut times; layers are grouped by their start. Opt-in; a scene without it renders byte-identical. See core/cuts/index.js PRESENTATIONS for the styles.

transitions.label: UNIFIED transitions (one surface): a boundary transition between two beats. `fx` routes to the right mechanism automatically (cut · seam · sting) via core/transitions/catalog.js, ambiguous basics (fade/slide/wipe) default to a cheap root cut; `mech:"seam"` upgrades to the real two-scene blend. Lowered to cuts/stings/seams at load. Inventory: `make transitions`.

at.label: Boundary time (s), a relative reference like "otherId.end+0.5" (core/timeline/relative-time.js), or "beat:<n>" (bare, 0-based) pinning it to the nth beat of the film's music grid (audio.beatSync, core/beats/index.js). The transition plays over [at, at+dur]

fx.label: Transition name (any from `make transitions`). Routed by mechanism: whipPan/crossWarp/cinematicZoom → seam; whip/punch/zoom → cut; glitch/chromaticSplit → sting; fade/slide/wipe/dissolve → cut by default (add mech:"seam" for the two-scene blend).

mech.label: Force the mechanism (default = auto). seam = two-scene GPU blend; cut = transform the scene root; sting = generative overlay.

dir.label: Travel direction: left|right|up|down, or a number of degrees (0=right, 90=up). A numeric dir only means anything for mech:"seam"; mech:"cut" still only knows the 4 names and throws on a number.

feather.label: Edge softness override, seam only (see seams[].feather). Omit for that unit's own baked default.

timing.label: Easing of the transition progress (default smooth = ease-in-out; linear = constant). Same curves as a cut/seam timing.

snap.label: false keeps this exact time when audio.beatSync is on. "beat"/"bar"/"downbeat" instead snaps THIS boundary to that pulse regardless of audio.beatSync.bar's own default (core/beats/index.js).

cx.label: Origin x, PER CENT of the frame, cut only (core/cuts/index.js formats it as `%` and defaults to 50)

cy.label: Origin y, PER CENT of the frame, cut only (core/cuts/index.js formats it as `%` and defaults to 50)

dist.label: Travel distance in px for a directional cut, cut only

colors.label: leak: up to 4 hex colours the leak is built from, sting only (seed only arranges them)

content.label: A flat {key: value} map. `{{key}}` inside any layer's `text`/`html`/`src` (at any nesting depth) is replaced by `content[key]` at build (core/engine/expand.js resolveContentSlots), so swapping copy or an asset path for a new customer/language/version is one map edited once. An unknown `{{key}}` is refused by name, both at `make validate` and at build.

cameraMove.label: Author sugar: { move, ...params } (or an array of them) → data.camera at expand time. Moves: slowPush | diveIn | panFollow | workspaceZoomOut | orbit | multiPhase | travel | truck | cameraShake | punchIn | driftHold | dollyZoom | followCursor | followLayer. `followCursor` is the one move that is DERIVED rather than typed: give it `"cursor": "<layer id>"` and it reads that cursor layer's own `path` and `clicks`, pushes toward each press, arrives just before it, holds, then releases, so the pointer stays the single owner of where the camera goes. `followLayer` tracks a layer's live box by id (`"id": "<layer>"`) instead of a fixed point, and resolves onto `cameraFollow`, not `camera`. This list is free text and has drifted before (it omitted travel and truck for months); CAMERA_MOVE_NAMES in core/camera-moves/index.js is the source of truth, and lib-test asserts the two agree. CAMERA BY ELEMENT: a diveIn, or any travel station, may name `"target": "#<layer id>"` instead of hand-typing `tx`/`ty`(/`to`): bakeCameraMove (core/engine/produce.js) resolves it once off the layer's own authored box (needs numeric x/y and a declared w/h or size), computes the largest scale that keeps the box plus an optional `margin` (fraction of the frame, default 0.06) inside the canvas, and prints the resolved numbers. Raw `tx`/`ty` on the same spec win and the target is dropped. `{"move":"diveIn","target":"#cta","margin":0.1}`.  A single leg may also declare `"beats": ["<id>", ...]` naming every `beats[]` id (below) it spans, when the move continues across a beat seam; core/engine/produce.js reports (never blocks) a move whose resolved window runs outside the beats it declares.

beats.label: Optional: ONE clock per beat, {id,start,duration}. Written by harness/author/assemble.mjs from the storyboard it already parsed (`id` reuses the html layer's own "scene<N>" convention). A beat's `id` becomes a relative-time target elsewhere in the scene ("beat:<id>.start"/"beat:<id>.end", plus an optional offset), for layer start, transitions[].at, cameraMove[].start and a bg window from/to (core/timeline/relative-time.js). A scene with no beats[] behaves exactly as it did before this field existed.

id.label: This beat's id, the name a "beat:<id>.start"/"beat:<id>.end" reference targets.

start.label: Beat start (s), or itself a "beat:<id>.start"/"beat:<id>.end" reference to another beat (plus an optional offset).

edits.label: Optional: a cut list of real footage, {id, src, in, out, ...}, lowered at expand time (core/engine/expand.js) into one `video` layer per entry, chained by "<previous id>.end" (core/timeline/relative-time.js) so an author never computes an offset by hand. NOT `cuts`: that key is the internal lowered output of transitions[] and is refused as an authored key (core/validate/validate.mjs). transitions[] still owns boundaries between cuts. A scene with no edits[] is untouched.

id.label: This cut's id, and the name the NEXT cut's start chains off ("<id>.end").

src.label: The source clip, a path under assets/

out.label: Trim-out point in the SOURCE (s). Must be greater than `in` (core/layers/video.js refuses an empty cut).

rate.label: Playback speed against the scene clock (default 1). The lowered layer's duration is (out-in)/rate.

audio.label: true, or {gain, duck}: pull this cut's own sound into the mix (core/layers/video.js, harness/media/clip-audio.mjs). Default absent = silent.

fit.label: Object-fit, only meaningful once `w`/`h` place this cut off full frame

w.label: Width (px), for a cut that is not full frame. Default: full frame.

h.label: Height (px), for a cut that is not full frame. Default: full frame.

x.label: X (px), for a cut that is not full frame.

y.label: Y (px), for a cut that is not full frame.

spectacle.label: The film's ONE loud moment, nominated: { at, of, device, why }. `device` is EITHER a shader sting name (flash | chromaticSplit | glitch | streak | whipPan | ripple | sdfIris | vortex | lens | dispersion | iridescence | cinematicZoom), written at `at` and injected · OR "<kind>:<name>" naming a cut, seam, kinetic preset, or another layer this film ALREADY builds (verified at `at`, never injected). The other half is what makes it real: with a spectacle declared the engine pulls EVERY competing amplitude dial in the film down to 55% (other stings, seams, composite-look strength, glow/beam intensity, kick scale), and exempts the layer named by `of` (and the device's own layer, when it named one). Naming the peak is a promise the rest stays restrained, and the engine keeps it. core/timeline/spectacle.js.

at.label: The second the moment lands on

of.label: The id of the layer the moment is ABOUT. It is the one layer the attenuation exempts.

device.label: A shader sting name (injected), or "<kind>:<name>" for a cut, seam, kinetic preset, or layer this film already builds (verified, not injected). Legal names span multiple registries plus this film's own layer ids, so intentionally NOT enumerated here: core/timeline/spectacle.js resolveDevice is the drift-proof guard.

why.label: What the moment is for, in one line. Required: a peak nobody can name is a volume setting.

lighting.label: The scene's KEY LIGHT: { x, y } in canvas px, plus optional { intensity } (default 1, scales every shadow at once). Read by the `shadow` modifier, which points each layer's shadow directly away from this point, so two cards either side of it throw their shadows in opposite directions, and one number re-lights the whole film. A light outside the canvas is normal.

intensity.label: Multiplies every shadow's opacity (default 1). 0 puts the lights out.

s.label: Where the camera stands, as the magnification of the canvas plane (1 = the default distance, 1.4 = closer). This is the camera's DEPTH, not a scale of the picture: with anything tilted in frame it dollies, so vanishing points move. There is deliberately no separate z key.

ease.label: Easing INTO this keyframe (default easeInOutCubic). Use "linear" on interior keyframes for a velocity-continuous multi-keyframe push (a chained ease-in-out pulses/shakes because it zeroes velocity at each keyframe). "through" carries velocity across the key from its neighbours.

easeOut.label: THE HANDLE LEAVING THIS KEY, a graph-editor control point for the segment that STARTS here. A handle NAME from the keyframe-handle registry (see `make arsenal`), or { "influence": 0-100, "speed": a number }. `influence` is how far along the segment the handle reaches, as a PER CENT of its duration. `speed` is how fast the value is moving AT this key, as a MULTIPLE of the segment's own average velocity: 0 is a dead stop, 1 is a straight line, 4 rushes out. A multiple and not px/sec, so ONE handle pair is correct for x, scale and rot at once and a property that does not change is not a division by zero. The far side of the segment is `easeIn` on the next key; a side that says nothing is the straight line. REFUSED beside `ease` on the same segment or `ease: "through"` on the same key: two answers to one question.

easeIn.label: THE HANDLE ARRIVING AT THIS KEY, a graph-editor control point for the segment that ENDS here. Same shape as `easeOut`: a name, or { "influence": 0-100, "speed": a multiple of the segment's average velocity }. `easeIn: "easyEase"` is the AE dead-stop arrival; `easeIn: "fling"` arrives fast and is what makes a swap read as one gesture rather than a dissolve. Pairs with `easeOut` on the PREVIOUS key.

roll.label: Camera roll about the view axis, degrees. Turns the whole frame without flattening anything tilted inside it.

p.label: The LENS: focal distance in px (default 1600; lower = wider). Not the camera's position. That is s. Keying both at once is the dolly zoom.

aspects.label: Per-aspect overrides for this camera keyframe

shader.label: shader: ambient WebGL look. Fields BEHIND content: flow/aurora/plasma/drift/mist/matrixDecode, plus domainWarp (marbled fBm), voronoi (cells) and metaballs (merging blobs). Overlay looks ON TOP (high track, intensity 0.6-0.9): vhs/crt/filmGrain/lightLeak + barrel/heatShimmer/ripple/kaleidoscope. Tune with speed · intensity · colors · seed

shaderKeys.label: shaderKeys: cycle ONE shader panel through several looks, on HARD CUTS. [{"t":2,"shader":"voronoi"},{"t":4,"shader":"nebula"}]. Before the first key the layer shows its own `shader`. Reach for this rather than stacking a layer per look: every canvas layer holds a WebGL context for the WHOLE film and browsers cap them near 16, and stacked windows crossfade, which dissolves two shaders into mud. `seed` · `intensity` · `colors` · `params` stay the layer's and apply to every look

t.label: Seconds from the layer's start, the same clock as `start`. NOT scaled by `speed`, which dials the field's own loop. Keys must run forwards

shader.label: The ambient field to show from `t` onwards. Same vocabulary as `shader` above

html.label: html: raw hand-authored HTML/CSS for the layer, inline (static; <script> stripped). Put it in a file with `src` instead when it is long enough to want reading, diffing or previewing

speed.label: clip: playback rate multiplier (1 = realtime; 0.5 = half speed)

typing.label: text: type it out at N chars/sec (true = 24) with a blinking caret

caret.label: typing: show the blinking caret (default true)

caretHold.label: typing: keep the caret after the text finishes

overscan.label: a full-bleed plane under perspective scales up just enough to cover the frame; false keeps its edges

typingColors.label: typing: each typed word flashes a colour from `colors`, then settles to the layer colour over `hold`

untype.label: typing: seconds into the layer at which the text starts DELETING backwards (backspace). Omit for forward-only typing.

untypeRate.label: untype: delete speed in chars/sec (default = the `typing` rate)

path.label: cursor: [{t,x,y,ease}] keyframes the pointer follows (x,y = absolute screen px when no layer x/y is set; relative to x/y if it is)

clicks.label: cursor: [t, …] local times to fire a click (dip + ripple)

filename.label: doc: filename shown in the card header (e.g. notes.md)

diff.label: doc: diff chip in the header (e.g. +18 -0)

blocks.label: doc: content blocks, {h,accent} heading · {body} mono lines · {code} · {bullets:[]}

bodySize.label: doc: body / code / bullet font px (default 30)

blockGap.label: doc: vertical gap above each heading block (default 22)

src.label: Path to the layer's source file: an image, a captured component (.json), a lottie (.json), or (on an `html` layer) a hand-authored fragment (.html) instead of the inline `html` string (exactly one of the two)

x.label: Left: px number, or relative "50%" / "50%-40" / center / left / right (resolved per aspect)

y.label: Top: px number, or relative "50%" / center / top / bottom (resolved per aspect)

w.label: Width: px number or "50%" of canvas

h.label: Height: px number or "50%" of canvas

anchorPoint.label: Which point of THIS LAYER'S OWN box x/y names. Default (absent) is the box's top-left corner, unchanged. "center" makes x/y the box's centre; needs a numeric w for a centre/right x, and a numeric h (or a text layer's `size`, estimated) for a centre/bottom y.

pin.label: Canvas-relative placement: edge/center (center = optical), or a rule-of-thirds power point

col.label: 12-col grid placement: "3" (one column) or "2-7" (a span) → sets x + w

gutter.label: Grid gutter px (default = half the safe inset)

ls.label: Letter-spacing (e.g. "-0.03em"); unset = auto optical tracking by size

raw.label: Opt out of the micro-typography pass (tracking/balance/kerning)

italic.label: Force italic on/off (default: serif is italic, others upright). italic:false = upright serif.

size.label: Font size (px). Up to 560 for frame-filling hero words (real launch films let a single word bleed the frame, scale contrast). The auto-fit safety + `make audit` still catch true overflow/clipping.

color.label: Glow color / text color (glow accepts true = the theme accent glow)

color2.label: Glow: the colour --glow-c crossfades TOWARD. Required when a layer keys that var, refused when it does not

emColor.label: <b> emphasis colour (default: brand accent, or inherit over an accent bg)

fit.label: Auto-size text down to fit w

duration.label: Window length (s), or a duration word (core/registry/vocab.js): instant | fast | medium | slow | luxurious

clock.label: group only: a local clock for the children, {duration, rate, loop: n | forever | pingpong, hold}; child track times are local to it (core/timeline/group-clock.js)

anim.label: Enter anim. EXACT names (core/timeline/clips.js ANIM): fade | up | rise | pop | scale | lift | defocus | slide-left | slide-right | slide-up | slide-down | wipe | wipe-left | wipe-right | wipe-up | wipe-down | iris | clock | none. Unknown names fall back to fade silently. There is no 'slide', and direction is part of the name, not a separate prop. A slide is named for the edge it comes FROM; a wipe is named for the edge its reveal TRAVELS TOWARD (wipe-up grows upward from the bottom; plain `wipe` = `wipe-right`).

out.label: driveClips exit anim (a NAME: fade | up | rise | ... , plays an entrance BACKWARDS, so the exit that CONTINUES the travel is the oppositely named one: anim:"slide-right" + out:"slide-left") · on a `video` layer: the OUT point in the source, seconds (a NUMBER; must be greater than `in`). The two never collide, a layer is one or the other.

exitDur.label: Exit window (s; 0 = hold to end), or a duration word (core/registry/vocab.js): instant | fast | medium | slow | luxurious

enterDur.label: Enter window (s, cut layers), or a duration word (core/registry/vocab.js): instant | fast | medium | slow | luxurious. It is ALSO the settle time of an `overshoot`: the ring is mapped into this window and lands exactly at rest at the end of it.

anticipate.label: ANTICIPATION: the layer winds BACK along its own travel axis by this fraction of the distance over ~3 frames, then goes straight into the entrance. 0.1 to 0.2 is the band motion designers quote. Real on the entrances that move through space or scale (rise/up, pop/scale, lift, slide-*); refused by name on fade, defocus, the wipes, iris and clock, which have no travel to bend. Every qualifying entrance gets this by default (core/engine/produce.js applyAnticipateDefault); `anticipate: false` is the OPT-OUT sentinel that strips it back off one layer, engine-doctrine/RULES/anticipate-default.md. A number is an explicit override of the theme-derived amount.

overshoot.label: OVERSHOOT AMOUNT: the entrance passes its resting pose by this fraction of the travel and rings down to it. 0.08 to 0.15 is the band motion designers quote. Replaces whatever amount the anim's own curve bakes in, so weight is tunable without changing preset. The settle time is `enterDur`. Same entrance set as `anticipate`.

step.label: ANIMATE ON TWOS: quantise this layer's own clock to N updates per second, so it holds each pose for several frames of the film. 15 is on twos in a 30fps film, 10 is on threes. Steps the entrance and the whole per-frame track pipeline together. Wrong on camera moves and on anything sliding across the frame, where it reads as dropped frames rather than as style.

idle.label: Ambient motion across this layer's SETTLED MIDDLE (between the enter ramp and the exit ramp), so a held frame stays alive without a hand-keyed motion track. A name, or { name, amp, period }. Off unless asked. Set the scene-level `idle` to opt a whole cast in, and `idle: "none"` here to opt one layer back out. Runs on TOP-LEVEL layers only, as the whole per-frame track pipeline does: put it on the group, not on a group child, and the group carries its children with it.

split.label: Kinetic split ('path' = SVG strokes, for the `draw` preset)

preset.label: Kinetic preset (split text; incl. chroma/swing/unfold) OR glow preset (bloom/halation/diffusion/rimLight/spotlight/chromatic/chromaCycle on a glow layer)

stagger.label: Per-unit delay (s), OR the three-dial object form { each, amount, from } that `parts[].stagger` takes too, so one vocabulary covers both. `each` is that same per-unit delay; `amount` is the TOTAL seconds the whole train may take and DERIVES the delay from the unit count, which is how a 90-glyph headline and a 6-word one hold the same beat; `from` is the ORDER the wave runs in: first (default, reads as typing) · center (the word arrives as one object) · last · edges · random (hashed, so a seek is exact) · or a unit index. e.g. {"amount":0.6,"from":"center"}

morph.label: text layer TextMorph: letters migrate `text`->word { to, dur, ease } (needs w+align:center, GSAP). svg layer shape-morph: one path melts into another { to, dur, spin, points, closed }.

trim.label: AE Trim Paths on any SVG path/stroke element: { start, end, offset }, each a fraction 0..1 of the path's real length (getTotalLength()). `start`/`end` pick the revealed segment; `offset` slides that segment around the path, wrapping on a closed loop, without changing its length. Each of the three is independently KEYFRAMABLE by naming `trimStart`/`trimEnd`/`trimOffset` in this layer's own `motion` array, composing with x/y/rot and riding the same per-segment ease (core/tracks/trim.js). Targets `el.__svgPath` (the svg layer's own path) or the first path-like SVG geometry found inside the layer.

fx.label: Named GSAP effect(s) from core/engine/gsap-effects.js: zoomBlur | {name,dur,ease} | [blurIn,float]. Entrances (zoomBlur/elasticIn/blurIn/spinIn/flipInX/bounceIn/clipUp/maskReveal/revealUp/expandIn/tiltIn/driftIn/glitchIn/foldIn), per-letter text (charFold/charTilt/charBlurCascade/charOvershoot, on split layers), loops (float/pulse/breathe/wobble). Pair with anim:none. There is no `fxOut`: the named GSAP exit family measured zero users and was deleted whole (engine-doctrine/MISTAKES.md #364); use `out` for an exit.

modifiers.label: Modifier stack applied to this layer, in array order, after every motion track: [{ "mixBlend": "difference" }]. Each key names a modifier from core/fx; an unknown name is a hard error, never a no-op. NOT `fx`, which is the named-GSAP-effect slot.

mixBlend.label: How this layer's pixels combine with what is painted behind it: "difference" or { mode: "difference" }. Refused on a group child: CSS blends against the nearest stacking context, which is the group, so it would reach nothing behind the group. Put it on the group.

squash.label: SQUASH AND STRETCH read off this layer's own velocity: true, or { amount: how far the travel axis stretches at full speed (default 0.18; 0.1 to 0.25 is the band motion designers quote), at: the speed in PX PER SECOND that earns the whole of it (default 1600) }. The perpendicular axis is squeezed by exactly the reciprocal, so the volume holds: scale both and it is a zoom, not a squash. Reads the same velocity sampler as the automatic motion blur and the ghost trail. Needs a `motion` track and is refused without one. Deforms along the DOMINANT axis, horizontal or vertical, because a non-uniform scale along an arbitrary axis needs a three-function transform and the tracks own `transform`. Refused alongside `kick`, which writes the same `scale` longhand. Wrong on a logo and usually on type, whose letterforms carry the deformation.

matte.label: A TRACK MATTE: another layer's luma or alpha becomes this layer's own alpha, white showing and black hiding. "sweepId", or { layer: "sweepId", mode: "luma" | "luma-inverted" | "alpha" | "alpha-inverted" }. `from` is accepted as a synonym of `layer`. `-inverted` flips which side shows (After Effects' Invert box), built from a second full-frame opaque mask XORed against the first (`mask-composite: exclude`), never a private inversion path. The general case of the whole wipe family, and the matte MOVES: it is placed and sized from the source layer's live box, so a source with a motion track drags its shape across this layer; animate the matte layer's own motion track and the reveal animates too. The source must PAINT AN IMAGE, because a CSS mask takes an image and a browser cannot read one live element's pixels as another's alpha: an `image` or `svg` layer's file, or a `rect` / `html` layer whose `bg` is a gradient. A paint / shader / three layer draws into a canvas and is refused by name. The matte layer itself stays out of the shot the ordinary way, `opacity: 0` on it; nothing here reads its rendered pixels. Needs an `id` on this layer, and refuses alongside `mask` / `progressiveBlur`, which write the same property.

lag.label: FOLLOW-THROUGH: this layer trails another layer's motion by a frame or three and overruns its stop before settling back. "cardId", or { of: "cardId", delay: FRAMES behind (default 2, 1 to 3 is the band), amp: the overrun as a fraction of the leader's velocity (0.05), freq: how often it wobbles (4), decay: the friction (8) }, after Dan Ebberts. Not `stagger`, which delays a SIBLING's whole entrance, and not `follow`, which pins to a live box with no delay: this carries the leader's own keyed offset, late. The leader needs a `motion` track; trailing a layer that is itself lagging is refused, because this reads keyframes and would land where nothing is. Refused alongside `plane`, which writes the same `translate` longhand. Wrong on a rigid board: a card that drags reads as jelly.

ghost.label: THE ONE EFFECT THAT READS TIME AS A MATERIAL: evaluate this layer's own `motion` track a few frames BACK and draw from the difference. "trail" leaves faded copies at the poses the layer just left; "blur" samples the same poses inside a single frame so the layer smears along its REAL direction of travel (unlike spinBlur/zoomBlur, which resample around a fixed point, or a `cx`/`cy` the author set). { mode: "trail" | "blur", k: samples 1..12 (default 6), back: lookback WINDOW in seconds, alpha: nearest copy's opacity, fade: per-copy falloff }. Needs a `motion` track and is refused without one; refused on a layer that draws into a <canvas>, whose pixels a clone does not carry. The copies are children of the layer, so cut, entrance, camera and ken ride along; a still layer renders identically to one carrying no ghost.

shadow.label: Cast a shadow AWAY from the scene's `lighting`, so two layers either side of the light throw their shadows in opposite directions: 30 (px of throw) or { dist, blur, spread, color, opacity }. `color` defaults to "auto" (read off the backdrop at t: the theme's ink over a light field, black over a dark one, the accent over an accent field) and also accepts a PALETTE ROLE name ("accent", "ink") so the shadow moves with the brand. Needs a top-level `lighting`; follows the layer's BOX, not its glyphs. Refuses alongside `elevation`/`shadow`/`glow` (they write the same property). Works on a group child, whose box is measured once at build and composed with its group's; the exception is a group whose motion track keys `w`/`h`, which reflows its children.

occlude.label: Hide this layer where another layer's box covers it: "cardId" or { by: "cardId" | [ids] | "above" | "below", pad: px grown around the occluder, invert: show ONLY the overlap }. "above"/"below" mean every layer painted in front of / behind this one, read from the scene's paint order, so the set is never a hand-written list that rots when a layer is added. The hole tracks the occluder's motion track (position, scale, rotation) and closes while it is outside its own window. Needs an `id` on this layer. Works on a group child; the exception is a group whose motion track keys `w`/`h`, which reflows its children and makes their measured offsets stale.

progress.label: Write the FILM's progress (0 at the first frame, 1 at the last) into a CSS custom property this layer's markup draws with: true (writes --film), "--bar", or { var, ease }. Not `vars`, which runs over the LAYER's own window; this is the scene's clock, so a runtime bar or a chapter dot re-times itself when the film is re-cut.

kick.label: Kick this layer on the film's own joints: true, or { on: "cut" | "seam" | "sting" | "any" | [kinds], scale: multiplier (default 1.06), frames: settle length in FRAMES (default 5) }. The times come from the scene's own cuts/seams/stings, so moving a cut re-times every kick in the film. Named `kick` because `punch` is already a whole-frame CUT STYLE.

upright.label:
AUTO-ORIENT: hold this layer UPRIGHT while the layer carrying it rotates. "wheel", or { of: "wheel" }, naming the ROTATING layer this one is carried by (normally the group it sits in). Parenting hands you the rotation for free and it is almost always wrong: photographs and words carried round a circle go upside down at the bottom, so the layout stops being readable exactly when the motion peaks. This cancels the carrier's rotation and NOTHING else, so the arrangement still swings this layer around the carrier's centre and only its orientation is held. Rotation only, not scale (a carrier that scales is moving toward the eye and its contents come with it; `plane` owns holding apparent size) and not skew. The angle is recomputed from the carrier's own `motion` keyframes, never read back off the rendered transform, so it stays pure in the frame index. The carrier needs a `rot` key in a `motion` track and is refused without one, because an entrance is composed by the clip pipeline and is not rotation this can read. Refused alongside `tilt`, which writes the same `rotate` longhand, and refused when it names this layer itself.

The After Effects name is Auto-Orient (engine-doctrine/CRAFT/AE-TECHNIQUES.md, technique 12).

tilt.label: Turn the layer out of the picture plane: { x, y, z } degrees about its own centre, projected through ONE camera shared by every tilted layer with the same parent. { dist } px is that camera's distance (default 1600, smaller = wider lens); { origin } is its vanishing point, "center" or [x, y] in canvas px. Siblings must agree on dist/origin or it is a hard error. On a group child the camera belongs to the group, not the canvas.

plane.label: Stand the layer at a DEPTH so the frame holds objects, not one sheet: -600 (px behind the picture plane) or { z: 240 } (in front of it, toward the eye). Sign is the CSS one. Two layers at different z move by different amounts when the camera trucks, which is parallax and is the whole point; every layer without it is at z = 0, where a camera move slides the entire composition rigidly. Turns the camera rig on by itself, exactly as `tilt` does. The layer changes apparent size (drawn at lens / (lens - z)) unless you set `hold: true`, which writes the scale correction every multiplane rig applies so the layer keeps the size you laid it out at and the depth shows up only as a different rate of travel. `hold` is OFF here and ON for the `depth` vocabulary. Refused alongside `kick` or `squash`, which write the same `scale` longhand. z at or past the lens (the camera's `p`, or `tilt.dist`, default 1600) is refused, and so is a group child, whose flat parent would project it through nothing. Put it on the GROUP.

alongPath.label: Set this layer's line of type ON A CURVE, and send it travelling along one: { curve: "arc" | "dip" | "wave" | "ramp", w, h, from, to, dur, delay, ease, anchor } or just "arc". `w`/`h` declare the box the curve is drawn in, and the viewBox matches it one-to-one so the layer's own font-size lands unchanged and nothing is measured. `from`/`to` are percentages ALONG the path and default to the same value, so the line simply sits on the curve and travels only when you ask; `anchor` says which end of the line sits at the offset. Pass `d` for your own path instead of a named curve. Refused with `split`, whose spans would be wrapped inside the SVG and render nothing.

wordSlot.label: One word of this layer's sentence swaps for the next while NOTHING after it reflows: { words: ["docs", "dashboards"], every: 1.1, swap: 0.26, chip: true, loop: false, at: "{}", delay: 0, rise: 0.42 }. The layer's own text carries the placeholder ("Ship {} in seconds"). Every candidate sits in the SAME grid cell, so the slot is auto-sized by layout to the WIDEST of them from the first frame, with no measurement and no font metric. `chip: true` gives it the accent plate with `--on-accent` ink, which is where the brand colour belongs. Refused with `split`, which would drive the same spans from a second clock, and refused with fewer than two words.

repeat.label: AE's Repeater: stamp this layer's OWN content { copies, offset: { x, y, rot, scale, opacity }, stagger, from }. `copies` (1..64) deep-clones the layer's built content into that many sibling cells. Each copy's transform ACCUMULATES from `offset` by its signed step `k` (translate x*k/y*k, rotate rot*k, scale compounding as scale^|k|, never scale*k); `offset.opacity` is AE's Start/End opacity, lerped across the ABSOLUTE copy index so the far end of the pattern fades regardless of `from`. `from` picks which copy is the unmoved origin: "start" (default, k=i), "end" (the last copy, k=i-(copies-1)), "center" (the middle copy, fans out both ways). `stagger` (seconds, default 0) delays each copy's own fade-in entrance, composing with whatever the LAYER's own `motion` is already doing, since every cell inherits the layer element's transform as its parent.

motionPath.label: Fly ANY layer along a path, and turn it to face the way it travels (GSAP MotionPathPlugin, AE's motion path + auto-orient): { path:'M0,0 C...' (or `d`, or `points`: an array of {x,y}, beziered by `curviness`), align, autoOrient: true|false, orientOffset (deg, an offset added while auto-orienting), curviness, from, to (0-1, which stretch of the path this tween crosses), dur, ease, delay }. `autoRotate` (GSAP's own name) still works underneath. Deterministic (closed-form position per frame).

physics.label: Velocity/gravity/friction scatter (GSAP Physics2DPlugin): { velocity, angle, gravity, friction, spread, dur }. On a split layer each letter gets an index-based angle spread (explode outward). Deterministic (no random).

parts.label: THE BRIDGE BETWEEN HAND-WRITTEN HTML AND THE ENGINE'S CLOCK. Dense per-CHILD choreography: stagger a named entrance across this layer's child elements (a bespoke SVG's bars/dots/paths, a group's cards, the rows of an `html` fragment) so a figure animates piece by piece. On an `html` layer this is how markup keeps the whole CSS surface AND still gets engine-driven, seekable per-element timing, instead of one opacity on the whole card. One spec { select, anim: growUp|widen|popIn|fadeUp|riseIn|drawOn, each, stagger, delay, ease, out, exitDur, exitEase } OR an array of them (bars, then line, then dots). `out: true` gives each part its paired exit (a translate continues, a scale reverses) anchored to the layer's end. `stagger` is a number of seconds OR the same three-dial object a split text layer takes, { each, amount, from }: `amount` caps the WHOLE train at a total time and `from` orders it (first | center | last | edges | random | an index). Pure (seeked GSAP).

comp.label: Composition name (type:"composition"). A FIRST-PARTY hand-authored per-beat GSAP timeline from core/compositions/index.js (a safe, hand-authored timeline-per-beat model). The JSON names the comp + passes DATA via `props`; the code lives first-party, so untrusted input cannot inject. Use for bespoke multi-tween motion `parts`/blueprints can't reach (a token travelling a path while a check draws). e.g. "pipelineFlow".

props.label: DATA passed to a `composition` comp (labels, numbers, accent). Treated as textContent/attr, never markup. e.g. { stages:["Input","Engine","Render"] }.

splitText.label: Masked LINE reveals (GSAP SplitText): { mask, stagger, dur, ease }. Each line slides up from behind a clip. Line-level only; use `split` for char/word. Do not combine with `split`.

circle.label: Lay the text CHARS on a rotating circular path (badge/seal). { radius: px, period: s/turn }. Set w = 2*radius so pin centres it.

effector.label: A falloff from a TRAVELLING POINT, driving the layer's own children: { select, path, radius, falloff, drives, sticky, release, overshoot }. `path` is a motion-key list ({t,x,y,ease}) in the layer's own coordinates, (0,0) at its top-left. `drives` names what the influence is spent on (scale|rotate|x|y|push|opacity) and by how much at full influence. `sticky` (seconds) is what makes it a painted TRAIL instead of a moving highlight: a clone holds what the pass did to it and releases over that delay. No keyframe lands on any clone.

smoothness.label: Range-selector smoothness, 0..1, default 1. How WIDE each split unit's transition band is, not its curve. 1 = the unit crosses its whole window continuously (every preset's historic behaviour). 0 = the unit SWAPS between states with no interpolation, so a glyph vanishes instead of scaling away. Requires `split`.

phaseStep.label: Per-unit phase offset for looping presets (wave/shimmerWave); ~0.12 = a crest travels the word

exit.label: WORD-BY-WORD EXIT on a split text layer: { preset, at, each, stagger, from, ease, presetOpts }. `at` is seconds after this layer's OWN start when the units start leaving; `preset` reuses the kinetic preset vocabulary (any name `preset` takes) but plays it REVERSED, so `up` sinks back down and fades, `blur` resolves back into blur. Left unconfigured, `each`/`stagger` derive from this layer's own arrival timing at 0.6x (an exit reads faster than the entrance it mirrors) and `ease` defaults to `easeInCubic` (an accelerating departure); an author can still override any of them. Requires `split`. e.g. {"at":1.2,"preset":"up"}

ransom.label: Comic/ransom cutout: each glyph a different face, paper swatch + torn edge (implies split:char; pair with fall/bounce). Object form: { palette: 'paper'|'color', sprites, accent, faces, swatches, cycle, stagger }. `sprites:true` uses REAL cut-out letter photos baked by `make ransom-sprites` instead of CSS tiles. `cycle` (s) re-rolls each letter into a different cutout of the SAME glyph in place

ransomSeed.label: Seed for the ransom cutout choices (defaults to the text, so the same word looks the same)

presetOpts.label: Per-preset knobs (e.g. gradient c1/c2, highlight color, blur px, tilt deg, wave amp, spring bounce/settle)

axis.label: Font-variation axis TRACK on a split text layer: { wght: [300, 900] } (or wdth/slnt/ital/a custom 4-letter tag) rides the SAME per-unit clock as `preset`/`stagger`, so it composes with any preset rather than needing one of its own. A bare number pins the axis; a [from, to] pair ramps it across the unit's own entrance. Requires `split`. e.g. {"wght":[300,900]}

gradient.label: STATIC gradient text fill via background-clip (distinct from preset:"gradient" which sweeps): { from, to, angle? }. angle 180 = top→bottom (a dark-top→light-bottom hero word). e.g. {"from":"#1c1613","to":"#f3763b","angle":180}

lookOpts.label: Composite-look knobs (core/looks/index.js): color · color2 · strength (0..1 master dial) · grain · vignette · warmth. Defaults reskin to the theme.

filter.label: CSS filter string OR a named grade preset (duotone/tritone/gradientMap/posterize/sepia/vignette, or chromaGlow) OR a composite LOOK (neon/dreamyHaze/vhs/crt/filmNoir/cyberpunk/thermal/lomo/… core/looks/index.js). One positional arg = strength 0..1 (e.g. "neon:0.9"); full knobs via lookOpts

blend.label: mix-blend-mode for a RAW `filter` on an adjust layer, e.g. "screen" for a bloom pass built from a blurred brightness copy. A named `kind` (bloom/blur/desaturate/…) already carries its own blend by default; state this only when writing `filter` directly with no `kind` to hang it on. core/layers/adjust.js.

falloff.label: a falloff: 1 at a source point, 0 with distance, multiplied against this layer through alpha. `{cx, cy}` place the source (0-1 of the box, default centre), `radius` is where it reaches 0, `feather` softens the ramp, `amount` caps how far it dims (1 = to nothing), `invert` flips it into a vignette. Owns no colour, timing or shape: it only dims what the layer already paints. Mutually exclusive with `mask`, which drives the same CSS property.

css.label: Raw CSS the layer vocabulary does not name (a box gradient via `background`, `clip-path`, a layered `box-shadow`, `backdrop-filter`, `mask-image`, pseudo decoration). camelCase keys in (`boxShadow`), applied once at build time. REFUSES opacity/transform/animation/transition/position/left/top/width/height/zIndex/pointerEvents (the engine owns and rewrites those every frame), use anim/motion/parts/vars/x/y/w/h/track instead.

becomes.label: Declare that this layer CONTINUES as another (by its `id`) across a boundary. A cut transforms one root and a seam blends two frozen stills; neither joins the CONTENT, so the only thing that truly connects two scenes is a form that persists. The named layer opens on THIS layer's final pose (centres matched, size matched by scale, rotation carried) and then animates away into its own geometry, so the handover is exact by construction instead of hand-aligned and hoped for. `becomesDur` (default 0.9) and `becomesEase` shape the handover. validate fails if the two do not meet at the boundary. See engine-doctrine/CRAFT/KEYED-MOTION.md.

becomesDur.label: Seconds the incoming layer takes to settle from the handed-over pose into its own (default 0.9).

becomesEase.label: Easing for the handover settle (default easeInOutCubic).

panWith.label: Share another layer's motion track by its `id`, on the SAME wall clock, from THIS layer's own origin. A pan of the page is not a camera move (a camera transforms the whole frame, scrim included), so moving a surface means moving its layers together. Copied as deltas and time-shifted by the difference in `start`, so each layer keeps its own position. Anything this layer declares WINS: state your own key at a shared time to peel away from the pan, and any key at a time the pan does not cover is kept. Worked example and the reasoning: engine-doctrine/CRAFT/KEYED-MOTION.md.

follow.label: Pin this layer to another layer's LIVE box, every frame: { id, edge, gap, dx, dy, from, to }. `anchor` places against the canvas and `becomes` hands one pose to another, and both resolve ONCE at build against numbers; neither can keep a label under a card that is moving, because the card's position after its motion track is only known at t. edge is center (default) · above · below · left · right, and `gap` is the space outside that edge. Centres are matched, not corners. `from`/`to` (seconds, optional) window the pin to that span of the film's clock; outside it this is a no-op. The pin lands BEFORE this layer's own motion track, so the follower may still have choreography of its own and it plays about the pinned position. This layer needs an `id` (it is placed by its own measured size). Following a layer that is itself following a third pins you to the middle one's UNPINNED position.

drive.label: AFTER EFFECTS EXPRESSIONS, as data, resolved fresh every frame. { wiggle, link, loop }. `wiggle`: { prop: x|y|rot, freq (Hz), amp (px or deg), seed, octaves } is deterministic seeded jitter. `link`: { from: "<layerId>.<prop>", mul, add, delay } is the pick-whip, this property copies another layer's own animated value, delayed (seconds) for follow-through; a link cycle is refused by name. `loop`: { mode: cycle|pingpong|continue, from, to } repeats this layer's OWN keyframes past `to` seconds instead of holding on the last one. `wiggle`/`link` take one spec or an array. `make arsenal Q="wiggle expression"` lists them.

style.label: cursor: the pointer's shape. arrow (default, unchanged pixels) · hand (hovering a control) · ibeam (hovering text) · block (a blinking terminal caret). `make arsenal Q="cursor style"` lists them.

styleAt.label: cursor: keyed style changes over the pointer's OWN clock, [{t, style}], e.g. arrow to hand on a hover then back to arrow after the click.

label.label: cursor: a name tag, { text, color }, attached lower-right of the point in `color` (the Figma multiplayer-cursor convention: a tag that matches its pointer reads as one person).

snapTo.label: cursor: snaps the pointer onto a named layer's LIVE box and keeps tracking it, so the click still lands after that layer moves. Write the id as a string, e.g. 'panel', timed off this layer's first `clicks` entry; or the array form [{t, id, edge, dur}] for an explicit time or edge (center default · above · below · left · right, dur 0.6s ease-in). Prefer this over `path` coordinates when landing on something the scene already places; refused by name for an unknown `id`, or a string with no `clicks` to take its time from.

carry.label: cursor: drag another layer along with the pointer, [{from, to, id}], all on the cursor's OWN clock. Bound at boot (core/engine/produce.js) onto the dragged layer's own `follow`, windowed to [from, to]. Refused by name for an unknown `id`, or one that already declares its own `follow`.

acrossBeats.label: This layer belongs to the FILM, not to one beat. Only meaningful under `sceneUnits`, where every other layer is wrapped with its beat and truncated at that beat's cut. Set true and the layer attaches flat to the camera instead, keeping its authored duration and its own exit, so it can survive a cut and change across it. This is how you author a continuous object in a cut film. It paints ABOVE beat content by default (its z-index is `track` or its array index, against wrappers at auto); give it `"track": -1` to sit behind.

edgeFade.label: Image: fade the LEFT+RIGHT edges into the bg (white by default). true or fade-width %

edgeFadeColor.label: Image: colour the edgeFade dissolves into (default #ffffff; set to the bg for dark scenes)

canvasFx.label: Image: Tier-2 Canvas pass baked once at build (deterministic). Name (halftone/dither/mosaic/pixelSort/stipple/ascii/edgeDetect/crosshatch) or { fx, cell, ink, paper, seed }. core/canvas/effects.js

roll.label: count: odometer wheels, each digit slides to its next value

unit.label: Count unit appended after the number (e.g. %, k, $B); raw ≥1e6 auto-compacts (2.5B) when no unit

anchor.label: Position relative to layer with this id

pad.label: Padding (px or CSS string), groups and text chips

children.label: Group children, text/image/count, or a nested group (layout by flow)

type.label: Child type. addGroupChild delegates to kit.buildLeaf, which dispatches the SAME layer registry as a top-level layer, so a child may be any layer type.

x.label: Child x inside a `free` group (ignored by flow layouts)

y.label: Child y inside a `free` group (ignored by flow layouts)

delay.label: Stagger this child's entrance N seconds into the group's window

contentStart.label: This child's CONTENT clock (video source time, typing, count, parts), N seconds into the group's window. May run before `delay` to pre-roll while hidden. Defaults to `delay`, clamped at the group's end

layout.label: Group layout: row | column | grid | free (children place themselves at x/y)

colw.label: Grid column width in px (layout:grid; default 1fr)

fitH.label: Max height (px) for multi-line auto-fit (with fit+w), binary-search font to fit

maxLines.label: Auto-fit safety: shrink a headline that wraps past this many lines (default 5)

items.label: align-items for a group (flex/grid): flex-start | center | flex-end | stretch | baseline

motion.label: Keyframe track, element choreography (pure in t). Offsets on the base position.

ox.label: Anchor point X at this key, as a PERCENT of the layer's own box. The pivot a scale or rotation grows out of, keyed so it can TRAVEL: `origin` is the static version and cannot move. Both endpoints of a segment must state it, or neither does.

oy.label: Anchor point Y at this key, as a PERCENT of the layer's own box. See `ox`.

rot.label: Rotation (deg), about the picture plane's own axis (CSS `rotateZ`).

z.label: Depth (px) at this key, toward (positive) or away from (negative) the eye, same axis and sign as the camera's own dolly. Animates a layer's DISTANCE, so unlike the static `plane` modifier a track can move a layer through depth over time. Needs the camera rig: keying it turns the rig on, the same way a `tilt` or `plane` fx does, because at z=0 with a flat parent it is projected by no lens and moves nothing.

rotX.label: Rotation (deg) about the horizontal axis (CSS `rotateX`), a layer tipping toward or away from the eye. Needs the rig; see `z`.

rotY.label: Rotation (deg) about the vertical axis (CSS `rotateY`), a layer turning like a swinging door. Needs the rig; see `z`.

blur.label: Gaussian blur (px) at this key. Keyable like every other pose property, and undocumented here until schema-drift learned to compare this block against the evaluator.

w.label: Width (px) at this key. The layer's BOX, not a scale: content re-fits instead of magnifying, which is how a sidebar collapses or a grid reflows. Needs a base `w` on the layer; state it on one key and every key inherits it.

h.label: Height (px) at this key. Same rule as `w`.

radius.label: Corner radius (px) at this key. Keyed alongside `w`/`h`, this is what turns a rectangle into a pill and then a circle: a pill is a rectangle whose radius reached half its height, a circle is a pill whose width reached its height. Unstated means unstated, the same as `w`/`h`/`track`: a track that never mentions radius leaves the layer's authored corner alone rather than starting to write one. A radius past half the box clamps silently in CSS, so judge it on a rendered frame and not on the number.

track.label: Z-order at this key. Depth over TIME: key it across a neighbour's track and the layer passes behind that neighbour and out again, which is how a ribbon orbits the thing it circles. Rounded to an integer when applied. Defaults to the layer's own `track`, or its index.

trimStart.label: AE Trim Paths `start` (fraction 0..1 of the path) at this key. Both endpoints of a segment must state it, or neither does (see `ox`); falls back to the layer's static `trim.start` otherwise.

trimEnd.label: AE Trim Paths `end` (fraction 0..1 of the path) at this key. Same both-endpoints rule as `trimStart`.

trimOffset.label: AE Trim Paths `offset`: slides the revealed start/end segment around the path (wrapping on a closed loop) without changing its length. Same both-endpoints rule as `trimStart`.

ease.label: Easing name (incl. spring, spring-bouncy, spring-stiff), ONE curve for the whole segment INTO this key; or a per-PROPERTY map (Separate Dimensions) so x and y on the same keys travel different curves, e.g. { "x": "linear", "y": "easeOutCubic" }. A map entry may also be { "easeIn": handle, "easeOut": handle } for that ONE property, symmetric with the whole-segment `easeOut`/`easeIn` below. A property the map omits still uses the segment's own curve. To draw the whole segment yourself, per side, use `easeOut` on the key before and `easeIn` here.

easeOut.label: THE HANDLE LEAVING THIS KEY, a graph-editor control point for the segment that STARTS here. A handle NAME from the keyframe-handle registry (see `make arsenal`), or { "influence": 0-100, "speed": a number }. `influence` is how far along the segment the handle reaches, as a PER CENT of its duration. `speed` is how fast the value is moving AT this key, as a MULTIPLE of the segment's own average velocity: 0 is a dead stop, 1 is a straight line, 4 rushes out. A multiple and not px/sec, so ONE handle pair is correct for x, scale and rot at once and a property that does not change is not a division by zero. The far side of the segment is `easeIn` on the next key; a side that says nothing is the straight line. REFUSED beside `ease` on the same segment or `ease: "through"` on the same key: two answers to one question.

easeIn.label: THE HANDLE ARRIVING AT THIS KEY, a graph-editor control point for the segment that ENDS here. Same shape as `easeOut`: a name, or { "influence": 0-100, "speed": a multiple of the segment's average velocity }. `easeIn: "easyEase"` is the AE dead-stop arrival; `easeIn: "fling"` arrives fast and is what makes a swap read as one gesture rather than a dissolve. Pairs with `easeOut` on the PREVIOUS key.

motionDelay.label: PER-PROPERTY timing on the motion track: seconds to delay ONE property's sampling, so scale can finish after position and rotation can settle after the travel (follow-through). A number delays every property; a map delays by name with "*" as its own default: { "rot": 0.1, "scale": 0.06 }. It shifts WHEN a property is read off the same track and changes no value and no keyframe.

motionBlur.label: Velocity motion blur (streak on fast moves; crisp when settled). true = half-shutter; a 0..1 number sets strength. On most layers it reads the layer's own motion track, so it needs one. On a three layer it instead samples the scene's own pose inside the canvas (litPlane), because a three scene moves inside a still box.

elevation.label: Physical depth 1–4 (ring + lit edge + stacked shadows)

glow.label: Ambient glow: hex color, or true for theme accent

intensity.label: Effect strength: glow opacity (0.05-0.6) · shader visibility (up to 1)

mode.label: beam layer: 'border' (a light travelling the border) or 'shine' (a sheen sweep)

thickness.label: beam layer: border-beam ring thickness in px

period.label: beam layer (shine): seconds per sheen sweep

viewBox.label: svg layer: the path coordinate system (default '0 0 100 100')

d.label: svg layer: the path `d` string (the from-shape when morphing)

fill.label: svg layer: fill colour (default var(--accent); 'none' for draw-on)

stroke.label: svg layer: stroke colour (default var(--accent) for draw-on)

strokeWidth.label: svg layer: stroke thickness in viewBox units. Works on any stroked path, not just a draw-on one (`draw.weight` still wins when both are set).

draw.label: svg layer: stroke draws itself on, then RESOLVES into the fill (stroke out, fill in) if one is given. {dur, weight, ease, fill, fillDur}. `fill` defaults to the layer's own `fill`; `true` means var(--accent); with neither, the mark stays an outline. `ease` defaults to easeOutCubic; easeInOutCubic is the AE Easy Ease standard.

pulse.label: glow: gentle breathing, sine period in seconds (amplitude <= 0.15; off by default)

flash.label: glow: one-shot attack-decay bloom. true, or {attack,decay,peak} seconds/peak<=0.45

hue.label: paint aurora: ONE hue (degrees) for every blob. Overrides `hues`, which is the per-blob list.

length.label: paint meteor: streak length in px

angle.label: glow spotlight: beam direction in degrees (0 = up, clockwise; default 150 = from above-left)

cycle.label: glow chromaCycle: seconds for the hue to sweep the full spectrum (default 6)

logotype.label: Text is part of a logo/brand mark, exempt from the CONTRAST bar only (WCAG 1.4.3)

keyClicks.label: Set false to silence the per-character key clicks a `typing` layer emits

keyGain.label: Gain of the per-character key click (default 0.3)

keyCue.label: Which cue a `typing` layer clicks with (default 'key')

aspects.label: Per-aspect overrides: { "9:16": { …props… } } merged over this layer at that canvas only

amp.label: Wave amplitude (paint) · three liquidBackground: swell height

rate.label: Glyph changes per second (paint matrix) · on a `video` layer: how fast the source runs against the scene clock (1 = real time, 0.5 = half speed)

in.label: video: the IN point in the source, seconds. Where the clip starts, not where the layer starts.

audio.label: video: pull this clip's OWN audio into the mix (default absent = silent, as before this prop existed). `true`, or `{gain, duck}`: gain scales the clip's sound (default 1), duck is the floor the music bed drops to while it plays (default 1 = no duck).

poster.label: video: a still shown before the first seek resolves. Optional; the engine seeks on frame one, so this is rarely visible.

react.label: Audio react: { band:'low'|'mid'|'high', prop:'scale'|'opacity'|'blur', range:[lo,hi] }, needs audio.spectrum

vars.label: Animate CSS custom properties over the layer's window: { "--p": [from, to] }

varsDur.label: Seconds the `vars` sweep takes (default 1). A NUMBER applies to every channel; an OBJECT keyed by channel name gives each its own, with `*` as that map's default

varsDelay.label: Seconds into the layer before the `vars` sweep starts

varsEase.label: Easing for the `vars` sweep (default easeOutCubic). A STRING applies to every channel; an OBJECT keyed by channel name gives each its own curve, with `*` as that map's default

crt.label: Cathode ray tube: softens and blooms what is BEHIND this layer, then lays scanlines and a corner falloff over it. { bloom: px, lines: 0-1, gap: px, scan: px, vignette: 0-1, tint }

glass.label: Frosted glass: blur what is BEHIND this layer. true = default, a number = blur px, a string = raw backdrop-filter

settle.label: three deviceShowcase: how the device is posed. Default (omitted, or true) is the REVEAL: it arrives at an off angle, pulls back by `travel` and eases to a held hero angle over `duration`, then holds. `false` gives the old TURNTABLE, an endless yaw/pitch sine that never lands, scaled by `spin`. `yaw`/`pitch` are the angle it settles ON when settling, and the sine's centre when not.

depth.label: Stand this layer at a named DEPTH so a camera move gives it parallax instead of turning the whole frame as one rigid pane: "far" | "back" | "front" | "near", each a fraction of the film's own lens, or a raw distance in px. It lowers to the `plane` modifier at boot WITH the scale correction held on, so the layer keeps the size you laid it out at and the depth shows up as a different rate of travel: far 0.57x, back 0.73x, front 1.18x, near 1.39x the picture plane's rate. Want the raw projection instead? Write `modifiers: [{ plane: { z } }]`. Refused on a group child, whose flat parent would project it through nothing. (On a `three` extrudeText layer the same word is the extrusion depth.)

timeRemap.label: TIME REMAP: keyframes on this layer's own CLOCK, so everything it does (its motion, size, idle, typing, count) speeds and slows together. Either a shape name ("whip" ramps 20% · 530% · slow, "hold" drops to 30% across the middle half, "freeze" holds the last pose, "rewind" plays then runs backwards) or your own keys: [{"t":0,"at":0},{"t":1.4,"at":0.3},{"t":2,"at":2}], where `t` is the layer's elapsed second and `at` is the second it believes it is. A repeated `at` freezes, a falling `at` reverses, and `t` only ever goes forward. The general form of `timeWarp`; declaring both is refused. A key also takes the graph-editor handles `easeOut` / `easeIn`, and their units land better here than anywhere: this segment's velocity IS a playback rate, so `speed: 4` on a handle means four times speed at that instant and `speed: 0` stops the clock dead at that key.

timeWarp.label: SPEED RAMP: an easing applied to this layer's own CLOCK, before any track reads it, so everything the layer does slows and speeds together (its motion, its size, its idle, its typing, its count). After Effects calls it Time Remapping. "easeInQuint" starts slow and whips to the end; "easeOutQuint" snaps in and glides out; "easeInOutCubic" ramps down and back up. Any easing name. The window itself does not move: only where inside it the layer believes it is.

kind.label: Adjustment layer: WHICH grade it lays over everything BENEATH it (every layer with a lower `track`). Its strength is `amount`, in that kind's own unit.

amount.label: Adjustment layer: the strength of its `kind`, in that kind's own unit (blur in px; desaturate 0..1; darken/brighten/contrast as a percentage). The CSS reads `var(--adjust)` times this, so `vars: {"--adjust": [0, 1]}` ramps the grade from nothing to here.

progressiveBlur.label: Directional blur fog on the backdrop that ramps toward an edge. { dir: top|bottom|left|right, layers: 2-12, max: px }. Fades a dense grid/list into an edge.

borderTrail.label: A glowing arc orbiting the layer border. { color, width: px, period: s/orbit, arc: deg }. CTA/end-card emphasis.

resample.label: LAYER AS TEXTURE: re-sample this layer's own pixels through a shader. Raster layers only (image/paint/shader). String, or {fx, amount, speed, seed}. amount may be [from,to] to animate. zoomBlur/spinBlur/directionalBlur are one blur primitive with the direction field the name picks: cx/cy (0..1, default 0.5/0.5) move the point zoomBlur radiates from or spinBlur pivots on (directionalBlur ignores it, its axis is angle); count (2..32, default 16) trades sample quality for render cost on all three.

raymarch.label: raymarch: a lit 3D subject rendered by a distance field (no geometry, no 3D engine). Give it a box the size the object should occupy; its surround is transparent. Dials: colors, intensity, speed (subject), spin (camera orbit), seed.

raymarchKeys.label: raymarchKeys: cycle ONE raymarch panel through several lit surfaces, on HARD CUTS. [{"t":2,"shader":"caustics"},{"t":4,"shader":"chromeGlass"}]. Before the first key the layer shows its own `raymarch`. Reach for this rather than stacking a layer per surface: raymarch is the most expensive primitive here and every canvas layer holds a WebGL context for the WHOLE film, and stacked windows crossfade, which dissolves two subjects into mud. `seed` · `intensity` · `colors` · `spin` stay the layer's and apply to every surface

t.label: Seconds from the layer's start, the same clock as `start`. NOT scaled by `speed`, which dials the subject's own animation. Keys must run forwards

shader.label: The lit surface to show from `t` onwards. Same vocabulary as `raymarch` above

spin.label: raymarch: camera orbit speed (0 holds the camera still while the subject moves)

seed.label: Deterministic seed for generative layers (shader / paint / raymarch)

colors.label: Palette for a generative layer (shader / raymarch), as hex strings

opacity.label: Base opacity for the layer's whole life, multiplied into the enter/exit fade

three.label: three: a real 3D scene (geometry, materials, lights, camera). For what an SDF cannot express: a device body with captured UI on its screen, extruded type from the real brand font, UI planes in depth, a point cloud. Posed absolutely from t, so it stays pure in n.

lines.label: three codeExtrude / codeDissolve / codeAssemble: the snippet, one string per line · the slab layout is derived from the real characters

screen.label: three deviceShowcase: image src mapped onto the device screen · three shatter: image mapped across the surface that breaks

breakAt.label: three shatter: seconds into the layer before the surface breaks

breakDur.label: three shatter: seconds the break takes

poles.label: three magnetic: 2 = a dipole (lines arc pole to pole), 1 = a single source (lines run straight out)

planes.label: three uiParallax: image srcs or {src,x,y,z} placed in depth

travel.label: three uiParallax: how far the camera dollies over the layer's window

rise.label: three litPlane: how far below its resting place the plane starts before it rises into frame

geometry.label: three object: what to build. {kind: sphere|box|torus|svgExtrude|textExtrude, ...}. sphere/box/torus take radius/w/h/d/tube; svgExtrude takes an SVG path `d` string (M/L/H/V/C/Q/Z only) plus scale/depth/bevelSize/bevelThickness/bevelSegments; textExtrude takes text/font (a typeface from `make glyphs`) plus the same bevel dials

path.label: svgExtrude: an SVG path `d` string, M/L/H/V/C/Q/Z commands only

depth.label: svgExtrude/textExtrude: extrusion depth in world units

bevelSize.label: svgExtrude/textExtrude: bevel size in world units

bevelThickness.label: svgExtrude/textExtrude: bevel thickness in world units

material.label: three object: the surface. {preset: glass|frostedGlass|metal|matte, color, ...}. glass/frostedGlass are MeshPhysicalMaterial (transmission, thickness, ior, roughness, clearcoat); metal/matte are MeshStandardMaterial (metalness, roughness)

color.label: Base tint (hex string). Defaults to the theme accent

thickness.label: glass/frostedGlass: refraction thickness in world units, default 0.6

ior.label: glass/frostedGlass: index of refraction, default 1.5 (real glass is 1.45-1.55)

clearcoat.label: glass: a second, always-glossy coat layered over the surface, default 1

envMapIntensity.label: How strongly the room's reflections show, default 1-1.2

env.label: three object: the reflection/refraction environment. Omitted, the procedural studio room every three scene already renders under; {image: src} replaces it with a real equirectangular capture (an already-tone-mapped jpg/png, not a raw .hdr)

image.label: An equirectangular (2:1) image src, preloaded like any other image the scene references

objectMotion.label: three object: keys the OBJECT's own position/rotation/scale through motionAt, the SAME sampler and eases `motion` uses on any layer. {t, x, y, z, rotX, rotY, rot, scale}; x/y/z in world units (x/y scaled from px by 0.01), rotX/rotY/rot in degrees

x.label: Horizontal offset (px-like units, scaled to world space)

y.label: Vertical offset (px-like units, scaled to world space)

cameraMotion.label: three object: orbits the SCENE'S camera around the object through the same motionAt sampler. rotY is azimuth (degrees), rotX is elevation (degrees), z adds to `dolly` for a push/pull

z.label: Added to `dolly` for this key, world units

pointSize.label: three pointCloud / globe / magnetic: point size in world units

phi.label: globe: rotation in radians at t=0. 4.8 puts the North Atlantic facing the camera

phiTo.label: globe: rotation it EASES TO, then holds. A constant spin turns the subject out of frame

theta.label: globe: tilt in radians, how far the pole leans toward the camera

mapSamples.label: globe: how many dots the land is sampled into (default 16000)

mapBrightness.label: globe: how bright the land dots are against the sea

diffuse.label: globe: how hard the day/night shading falls across the sphere

dark.label: globe: overall darkness of the unlit side

scale.label: globe: how much of its box the planet fills (1 = default)

markerSize.label: globe: size of the two endpoint markers

origin.label: TRANSFORM ORIGIN: which point a scale or rotation grows OUT OF. A CSS value: a keyword pair ("top left"), a length pair ("40px 12px") or percentages ("0% 50%"). A scale from its own centre explains nothing; one from the point the thing came from explains the relationship. · ON A `three` GLOBE ONLY it is a different prop entirely, [lon, lat] of the route's start, and the two share only the word.

dest.label: three globe: [lon, lat] of the route's end

spinFrom.label: three globe: rotation in radians at t=0

spinTo.label: three globe: rotation it EASES TO, then holds. A constant spin turns the subject out of frame; this arrives and stays

spinDur.label: three globe: seconds the settle takes

sunFrom.label: three globe: sun longitude in degrees at t=0. The terminator is computed from it, so the lit land and the lit sea cannot disagree

sunTo.label: three globe: sun longitude at the end of the layer. Decreasing sends the terminator WEST, which is the direction the real one moves

sunLat.label: three globe: the sun's declination in degrees. The seasonal tilt of the day/night line

dawnWidth.label: three globe: how soft the terminator is, in cosine units. 0 is a hard edge, 0.22 is a band of dawn

arcHeight.label: three globe: how far the route lifts off the surface, as a fraction of the radius (default 0.18)

drawStart.label: three globe: local time in seconds at which the route begins drawing (default 0)

drawDur.label: three globe: seconds the route takes to draw. The aircraft rides the SAME parameter, so the line and the marker cannot disagree (default 4)

params.label: Per-effect parameters
params.note: shader only: up to four numbers, meaning whatever that effect's branch says. `bands` reads them as (slat count, angle in turns, glow radius, glow softness).

params2.label: Per-effect parameters, second vector
params2.note: shader only. `bands` reads it as (field: 0 linear / 1 radial / 2 box, centre x, centre y as a fraction of the frame from the middle, light sign).

params3.label: Per-effect parameters, third vector
params3.note: shader only. `bands` reads it as (gradient: 0 along the bands / 1 on its own axis, that axis in turns, per-band convergence, band phase).

params4.label: Per-effect parameters, fourth vector
params4.note: shader only. `bands` reads it as (mirror the bands about the field centre, light x offset, light y offset, light shape: 0 round or oval / 1 bar / 2 rounded).

params5.label: Per-effect parameters, fifth vector
params5.note: shader only. `bands` reads it as (the light's y radius as a fraction of its x radius, the light's angle in turns, within-band shading depth, how much of the per-band convergence step leans across the band).

params6.label: Per-effect parameters, sixth vector
params6.note: shader only. `bands` reads it as (light ring radius, light star points, light star depth, zoom around the light). Every field is 0 for the behaviour that predates them.

words.label: Optional per-word timings [{t0,t1}], aligned to this line's markup-stripped word list. Drives every captionStyle. Omit and core/type/captions.js distributes the line proportionally to word length, which still reads as intentional karaoke. Written for you by harness/media/vo-captions.mjs from a TTS sidecar.

pin.label: Where this caption sits, in the SAME placement grammar as a layer (core/engine/boot.js resolveCoords): center | top | bottom | left | right | top-left | top-right | bottom-left | bottom-right | thirds-*. Omit and films/scene/scene.css places it, which is the bottom band it has always used.

x.label: Left edge in px, or a relative form: "50%", "50%-40", "center", "left", "right", "third1", "third2". Edge keywords resolve against the SAFE box for this destination, so an edge-pinned caption can never land under platform chrome. Setting x releases the stylesheet's right edge.

y.label: Top edge in px or a relative form (see x). The two-line caption band (core/layout/safe.js CAPTION_LINES) is the extent "bottom" subtracts, so pin:"bottom" lands the band inside the safe box rather than hanging it off the line.

w.label: Caption box width in px or "60%". Omit and the stylesheet's margins decide.

align.label: Text alignment inside the box: left | center | right. Default center.

size.label: Font size in px for this caption only. Default is the skin's (46 plain, 64 pop/styled, core/layout/safe.js CAPTION_SKINS). Changing it changes the band this caption reserves.

grain.label: Opt in to the in-engine canvas grain (default off, matching the ffmpeg pass)

audio.label: Sound. Every film should have some, and silence should be a decision you write down (`make audio-check D=<file>`). Mixed by internal/audio/audio.go; beds picked by core/audio/select.js. The CUES are synthesized and carry no licence (core/audio/kit.mjs), but the MUSIC beds under assets/music/ are downloaded third-party tracks. Check assets/music/credits.json before any commercial release. See engine-doctrine/CRAFT/SOUND.md.

music.label: Music bed. Silence is the default, so this is opt-in: "auto" (audio-select picks a bed by mood), a baked bed NAME (calm | warm | tense → assets/music/<name>.wav), or a path to a .wav. Omit for no bed. `make validate` resolves it against assets/music/ and the scene dir and warns if it will not.

auto.label: Auto-pick a music bed AND auto-derive sfx cues from cuts/stings (core/audio/select.js). Same as music:"auto".

musicGain.label: Music bed level (0 = muted, ~0.5 typical). Ducks automatically under VO.

musicDuck.label: Duck floor: how far the bed drops while VO plays (0..1, e.g. 0.15).
