loudness.label: Integrated loudness target in LUFS (negative, e.g. -14 for social). Absent = peak-normalize only.

vo.label: Voice-over WAV path (resolved against the scene dir + repo root). A named-but-missing file fails `make validate` (the mixer would silently drop it).

voWords.label: VO word-timing sidecar JSON: [{ "w": "hello", "t": 1.2 }], drives word captions.

sfxGain.label: Master multiplier over EVERY sfx cue (authored + auto-derived).

bridges.label: Sound bridges, J-cuts and L-cuts. A bridge is a texture that crosses a picture change instead of stopping at it: a J-cut starts the next shot's sound BEFORE its picture, an L-cut lets the last shot's sound run UNDER the new one. It is the one continuous object that costs the picture nothing, so a film whose beats are visually unrelated is still held together. Each bridge names a JUNCTION, never a timestamp, so retiming a beat moves the sound with it. Resolved by core/audio/bridges.js, mixed by internal/audio/audio.go. See engine-doctrine/CRAFT/SOUND.md §2.

bridge.label: "j" = the audio leads (new sound over old picture) · "l" = the picture leads (old sound under new picture).

at.label: The junction, as "<kind>@<index>": cut@1 · seam@0 · sting@2 · junction@3 (junction = all of them merged). The index counts in TIME order within that kind. An index the film does not have fails the render and lists what it does have.

sound.label: The texture: a bed name ("tense" → assets/music/tense.wav), a synthesized cue name ("loading" → assets/sfx/loading.wav), or a path to a .wav. Looped to fill the span. A source that is not on disk FAILS the render. A bridge that never plays is not a quieter film.

lead.label: J-cut only, required: seconds of sound that arrive before the picture cuts. A lead longer than the beat before the junction is rejected, not clipped.

lag.label: L-cut only, required: seconds the sound keeps running after the picture cuts. A lag past the next junction is rejected.

span.label: How long the sound holds on its OWN side of the junction (after it for a J-cut, before it for an L-cut). Default: to the neighbouring junction, or the edge of the film.

fade.label: Equal-power crossfade at both ends of the span, seconds (default 0.35). A bridge never butts: the point is that the ear crosses over, not that a second file switches on.

duck.label: Floor the MUSIC bed drops to under this bridge, 0..1 (default 1 = no duck). Setting it is what makes the join a cross rather than a stack: the bed dips on the same curve the bridge rises on.

cues.label: Sound-effect cues, each { t, and then either `name` for a baked sample or `voice` + `params` for a synthesised one }. THIS is where cues live (the engine reads `audio.cues`); there is no top-level `sfx`.

t.label: Cue time (s), or a relative reference like "install.end+0.2" (core/timeline/relative-time.js) so the cue pins to the MOMENT a layer arrives instead of a number an author has to recompute by hand every time that layer moves.

name.label: Cue name: a baked sample under assets/sfx. OPTIONAL when `voice` is set, and exactly one of `name` or `voice` must be present. A sample is a recording nobody can tune and a fresh clone does not have; prefer `voice`.

voice.label: Synthesised voice: baked on demand by generators/media/voice-cue.mjs from core/audio/kit.mjs's CUES table, cached under assets/sfx/ by a hash of (voice, params), then played as an ordinary named sample. Deterministic, needs no shipped asset. Every name here is a live CUES key (core/validate/validate.mjs checks the two never drift); a voice not in CUES is refused at validation, not silently dropped.

params.label: Synth parameters for `voice`, all numbers, unknown keys refused at validation: freq (Hz, rescales every tone layer keeping the voice's own intervals), gain (masterGain), attack, decay (multipliers on the voice's own values, 1 = unchanged), seed. Omitted keys take the voice's preset value.

spectrum.label: Precomputed spectrum sidecar JSON for audio-reactive layers (layer `react:{}`).

beatSync.label: Snap the film's picture joints to the music's pulse. `true` takes the grid `make beatmap` wrote beside audio.music (assets/music/<bed>.beats.json); an object may set `grid` (an explicit .beats.json), `maxShift` (how far a joint may travel, default 0.12s) and `bar` (snap to downbeats, not every beat). Cuts snap their time and seams snap the centre of their blend; stings never snap, because an author offsets one from its cut on purpose. A grid that is missing, empty or below confidence 1.6 FAILS the render rather than quietly leaving the film unmatched. core/beats/index.js, engine-doctrine/CRAFT/SOUND.md.

grid.label: Explicit path to a .beats.json (default: derived from audio.music).

maxShift.label: How far a joint may travel to reach a beat, in seconds (default 0.12). Beyond it the joint stays where it was written and the run says so.

bar.label: Snap to downbeats (bar lines) instead of every beat.

silent.label: Render with NO audio track at all. A real device (a film can be better mute) but never a shrug: pair it with `_why`. A film with no sound and no stated reason is not silent by style, it is unfinished, and `make audio-check` says so.

_why.label: One sentence saying what the silence is DOING (e.g. "autoplays muted in-feed; the type carries it alone"). Required alongside `silent:true` by `make audio-check`. Same mechanism as `authoring._why`: waiving costs a sentence, and that cost is what turns a reflex back into a decision.

tactile.label: Opt in to TACTILE sound design (core/audio/tactile.js): the engine reads its own timeline and voices the MOTION, not just the junctions. A layer arriving thuds or plucks by its size and how far it travels, a camera move whooshes, a counter plucks on the number's own easing curve, a `parts` stagger plucks per part, and a declared `spectacle` gets a riser that ends on the moment. Implies `auto`, so cuts and seams keep their CUT_CUE voicing. Off by default: silence stays the engine default and no existing mix changes. An object tunes the density rules: { maxPerSec (5), minGap (0.05), gain (1), riserLead (0.9) }.

maxPerSec.label: Most derived cues allowed in any one second. Default 5. The lightest cue in an over-full second is dropped first, so a headline survives and a hairline does not.

minGap.label: Two cues closer than this flam into one smeared attack, so the lighter one is dropped. Default 0.05s.

gain.label: Multiplier over every derived motion cue. Default 1. Structural cut/seam cues are unaffected (use `sfxGain` for those).

riserLead.label: How long before `spectacle.at` the riser starts, which must match the baked riser's own length. Default 0.9s.
